title: staged-token-commit-cohorting-and-kv-reservation
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: streaming TTFB and tail latency remain sensitive to two correlated effects: (1) kernel warmup / KV cache misses when concurrent streams touch cold KV entries, and (2) bursty flushes that create temporary contention on compute kernels. This PR introduces a staged-token-commit model plus a cohort-based emitter scheduler and a lightweight KV reservation mechanism to reduce first-byte latency and smooth tail spikes.

What changed (high level):
- Staged token commit: instead of forcing a full commit on every emitter flush, the emitter can now perform a 'soft-commit' that makes tokens visible to the network path earlier while final write-through to persistent KV happens asynchronously. Soft-commits are serialized per-stream to preserve consistency and can be configured with a soft_commit_timeout.
- Cohort emitter scheduler: streams are grouped into short-lived cohorts (50–250ms windows) based on recent TTFB deadlines and sequence progress. Cohorts are scheduled as a unit to allow contiguous kernel execution and reduce kernel context switches.
- KV reservation table: when a cohort is created, the scheduler attempts to reserve KV cache slots for the cohort's hot keys (kv-reserve hints emitted by the model runtime). Reservations are soft (best-effort) and give scheduling hints to prefetch threads to warm GPU DRAM/TLB footprints before tokens are emitted.
- Credit smoothing: we apply exponential smoothing to per-stream credits to avoid oscillatory credit injections that caused microbursts. Smoothing is tunable by the new emitter.credit_smooth_alpha config.

Why this is different: previous approaches focused on flush cadence and token batching; this PR combines a visibility-latency optimization (soft commits) with scheduling-level grouping plus cache reservation hints. The combination lets us emit earlier without regressing correctness and reduces both median and 99th percentile first-byte latency under mixed workloads.

Results:
- End-to-end experiments on perf-lab (64-stream mixed prompt mix) show median TTFB reduced by 9% and 95th/99th percentile TTFB reduced by 17% / 24% respectively compared to baseline with the same batch size.
- KV cache miss rate on the hot-key set dropped ~13% during warmup phases.
- CPU side latency variance reduced leading to 12% fewer scheduling stalls observed in kernel telemetry.

Backward compatibility and safety:
- Soft-commit is behind a runtime flag and defaults to off for dedicated/private installs; the flag is enabled by default in the hosted experimental pool.
- When enabled, soft-commit preserves ordering semantics: tokens are visible in-order per-stream; durable KV write is deferred but reconciled on background worker. In the rare case of node crash before background write, we detect and replay from the emitter's sequence checkpoint.

Testing and benchmarks:
- Unit tests: emitter soft-commit state machine (race conditions, timeouts), cohort lifecycle, KV reservation bookkeeping.
- Integration tests: long-tail simulation harness, perf-lab deterministic replay with recorded request traces.
- A/B perf runs executed against canary region (us-west-2) for 48 hours. Results attached in perf/39977/summary.csv.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Canary in hosted experimental pool (2% traffic) for 24h. 3) Expand to 20% and enable KV reservation prefetching. 4) If stable, enable soft-commit by default and monitor linear alerts ENG-1478.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-1478)
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Perf lab numbers attached
- [x] Feature flagged and config knobs added
- [x] Docs/observability (dashboard widgets + traces)

Migration notes:
- Operators should review emitter.credit_smooth_alpha and emitter.soft_commit_timeout; defaults keep behavior unchanged if the feature flag is off.

Release notes:
- Introduces staged token commit and emitter cohorting to reduce streaming first-byte latency and tail. Disabled by default in Dedicated/Private; opt-in via feature flag.
commits_summary: 3 commits: [feat: staged soft-commit + state machine; perf: cohort scheduler implementation; ops: kv reservation table + telemetry + feature flag], each commit contains targeted unit tests and small API bumps (Emitter::soft_commit()).
review_comments: Daniel Kim: Left a few nit comments but major question on durability: if a node crashes after soft-commit but before background write, how do we ensure no tokens are lost? Please add an integration test or link the replay guarantee.

Asha Patel (author): Added a reconciliation pathway. On startup, the emitter checks sequence checkpoints and replays any soft-committed tokens to the background writer. Added integration test tests/integration/stream_cohort_replay.rs to validate replay under crash simulation.
Maya Thompson: Can we avoid increasing CPU prefetch worker contention? Reservation looks promising but we should gate aggressive prefetches when system CPU utilization > 75%. Please add a backoff.

Asha Patel (author): Added a soft backoff that observes host-level cpu_utilization metric and reduces prefetch concurrency; default threshold set to 0.75 and configurable via kv.prefetch_cpu_backoff_threshold.
Evan Ruiz: Observability looks good, but please emit a cohort_id tag on span to correlate kernel traces with emitter cohorts.
Asha Patel (author): Added cohort_id to tracing spans in cohort_scheduler and updated emitter_metrics doc.
Daniel Kim (approved): Tests look good and perf numbers are convincing. Approving for squash-merge.
Maya Thompson (approved): Approved after backoff change.
